[shr-00001] When the task is to 'look at' an object and the object is visible or accessible in its current location, then examine the object in place (e.g., 'examine <object>') instead of taking it unless the object is hidden or requires being picked up to be viewed.
[shr-00002] When an object is already visible and accessible, and repeated examination of its location yields no new information or environmental change, then stop examining the location and proceed to examine or interact with the object directly.
[shr-00008] When the task is to 'examine <object> with <tool>' and both the object and the tool are visible and accessible, then directly perform the action 'use <tool> on <object>' to fulfill the task requirement, without first using the tool alone or interacting with unrelated objects.
[shr-00021] When the task is to 'look at <object> with <tool>' and the object is not in the correct relative position (e.g., not under the desklamp), then first adjust the object's position to satisfy the spatial condition before applying the tool directly to the object.
[shr-00023] When the task is to 'look at <object> with <tool>' and the object is visible and accessible in a different location than the tool, then apply the tool directly to the object from the object's location (e.g., 'use <tool> on <object>') without first moving the object or the tool, provided the tool is accessible.
[shr-00026] When both the object and the tool are visible and accessible, and the object is already in the correct spatial position (e.g., under the desklamp), then directly apply the tool to the object (e.g., 'use <tool> on <object>') without activating the tool in isolation (e.g., 'use <tool>').
[shr-00040] When the tool requires activation (e.g., turning on) and the object is already visible and in the correct spatial position (e.g., 'under the desklamp'), then activate the tool as part of the direct application to the object (e.g., 'use desklamp on vase') instead of activating the tool in isolation.
[shr-00041] When the task is to 'put <object> on <receptacle>' and the object is visible and accessible, then directly take the object and place it on the receptacle without unnecessary intermediate steps.
[shr-00047] When the task is to 'put <object> in <receptacle>' and the task specifies multiple instances (e.g., 'two alarmclock'), then systematically retrieve and place each instance one at a time, ensuring each is moved to the receptacle before proceeding to the next.
[shr-00051] When the task is to 'put <object> on <receptacle>' and multiple instances of the object are found in the same location, then retrieve and place all instances from that location before moving to other locations to minimize backtracking and maximize efficiency.
